title: Multiprotocol internal ingress terraform module: TLS passthrough + termination, cert fabric, health orchestration
creator: Iris Kwan
description: Create a single Terraform module that provides a multiprotocol internal ingress for Private deployments. The module must support: (1) NLB listeners for TLS passthrough to customer backends, (2) ALB for HTTP(s) termination where we need path/host routing and WAF integration, (3) dynamic certificate selection via ACM and Vault-stored certs (cert fabric), (4) configurable session affinity (cookie + source IP fallbacks), and (5) active health orchestration to minimize cross-AZ failover blast radius during upgrades. This ticket owns the module design, provider-agnostic Terraform code (AWS-first), integration tests, upgrade/rollout strategy, and automated healthcheck tooling hooks for Redwood Private packages.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes clear inputs: network (subnet IDs), listener map (protocol, port, target type), cert_source (acm|vault), affinity_policy (none|cookie|ip), health_probe config, and rollout_policy (canary|weighted|immediate)
Module deploys to a sandbox VPC and provisions both an NLB passthrough listener and an ALB termination listener behind the same DNS entry using Route53 weighted records for canary traffic

Automated certificate rotation path: create new cert in ACM or Vault, stage it on "blue" listener, switch weights to blue, then destroy legacy cert after 7-day grace period — all via terraform plan/apply

Health orchestration: when an instance fails cross-AZ checks, module reduces weight to that AZ and triggers a gradual traffic shift; tests simulate AZ failure with >95% traffic reconfiguration within 2 minutes
Session affinity works for both TCP passthrough targets (NLB) and HTTP targets (ALB) with documented trade-offs and recommended defaults
Zero-downtime upgrade documented and validated in CI (integration plan runs traffic simulation and asserts no 5xx spike >0.5%)
implementation_plan: Design phase: finalize module interface and default opinions; get PM + Security sign-off on cert fabric access patterns (2025-11-18 to 2025-11-20)
Prototype: build AWS-only PoC with nlb passthrough + alb termination in sandbox (2025-11-21 to 2025-11-25)
Iterate: add cert rotation lifecycle, session affinity options, and health orchestration hooks; expose metrics for Console (2025-11-26 to 2025-12-03)

Docs & rollout: add README, example overlay for Private installer, migration guide for existing customers, and ops runbook (2025-12-09 to 2025-12-10)
Release: merge module, cut release tag, bump Private package that consumes it
technical_notes: We will use aws_lb (ALB) + aws_lb_target_group for HTTP terminator. For TLS passthrough we use aws_lb (NLB) with target type ip for ECS tasks / private IP targets.

Certificate fabric: where possible prefer ACM-based certs for ALB listeners. For workloads that require customer-managed keys or mTLS, integrate Vault PKI flow and upload to AWS Certificate Manager using import flow or keep certs on ALB via SSM aromatic syncer (documented pattern).

Session affinity: ALB cookie-based stickiness is straightforward. For NLB (TCP) we recommend a dual approach: enable proxy_protocol where supported + source_ip affinity in target group. Document limitations for container re-scheduling and L4 load balancing.

Health orchestration: implement a "weight controller" Terraform approach that emits an AWS Lambda-backed step function (minimal infra) to adjust Route53/ALB weights during probe failures. Prefer a declarative opt-in hook so large customers can disable the lambda and use their orchestration.

Rollout strategy: support weighted target groups for listener swaps; terraform should create new target group + register new instances, then gradually shift ALB/NLB weights via route53/traffic policies before removing old TGs. Ensure the plan shows weight diffs clearly to avoid surprise destroys.

Simulate AZ outage by cordoning nodes and verify weight controller rebalances within 2 minutes

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Certificate import/removal can cause listener flaps if not staged properly. Mitigation: implement blue/green staging for certs and require manual approval gate for customers with compliance needs.

Risk: Terraform-managed weighted traffic changes may conflict with other automation. Mitigation: module exposes opt-out for weight controller and provides a small API (SNS topic) to coordinate external systems.
Risk: Sticky sessions may concentrate load and skew autoscaling. Mitigation: document trade-offs and recommend short TTLs or stateless session strategies where possible.
